As a result, up to 26.31% PCE with impressive durability (ISOS T 90 lifetime > 500 h) is yielded for the WH07-based device, which ranks amongst the best results for n-i-p PSCs. These findings demonstrate that the synergistic intra- and inter-molecular geometry modulation is a promising approach for the comprehensive optimization of molecular semiconductors in high-performance perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Hydrolysis gaming chemistry to regulate TiO2 deposition for high-performance perovskite solar cells
Force-activated enzyme-laden hydrogel enables mechanical and biochemical synchronous regulation for osteoarthritis therapy
In-situ co-growth LiF/LiBr rich SEI for the prevention and remediation of dead lithium
abstract: Solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) instability and dead Li accumulation remain persistent challenges for lithium metal batteries. Although considerable efforts have been devoted to optimizing the SEI composition, the issue of dead lithium accumulation remains largely neglected. Herein, we design a covalent organic framework (COF)-based dual-functional separator to regulate the chemical composition of the solid electrolyte interphase to form a LiF/LiBr-rich SEI, while simultaneously introducing Br - /Br 3 - redox couple in-situ at the interface for dead lithium reactivation. Both theoretical and experimental evidence demonstrate that the introduction of TPPA-Br triggers cleavage of the C-Br bond, leading to the in-situ formation of an ionically conductive LiF/LiBr-rich SEI. The LiF can promote uniform lithium deposition and prevent dead Li formation. Meanwhile, the LiBr can result in Br - /Br 3 - redox couple, which further chemically reactivates Li 2 O and electrically isolates Li 0 , mitigating capacity decay associated with dead Li accumulation. Consequently, Li||LiFePO 4 cells employing TPPA-Br functional separators display good cycling stability over 1200 cycles with 90.1% capacity retention at 1 C (1 C=170 mA g -1 ), confirming the practical potential of this interphase-regulation strategy.

title: Channel intercalation in triangular lattices: reshaping the paradigm of lightweight conductors through carbon nanotube fiber chemistry
Coordination-engineered Cu sites in conductive MOFs steer CO2 electroreduction toward ethylene
High-energy hydrogen radical bullet penetrates barriers for urea electrosynthesis
Metastable C–Mo–O/Ni sites mediate partial oxidation of methane via O* species-assisted C–H bond activation pathway
abstract: The partial oxidation of methane (POM) is hampered by the high kinetic barrier of C-H bond activation, which demands high operating temperatures, and catalyst surface oxidation induces detrimental deactivation. This paper describes that the dual role of molybdenum carbide (MoC x ) enables facile methane activation and imparts oxidation resistance to Ni-based catalysts. We found that MoC x modifies the reaction mechanism by altering oxygen adsorption, becoming the preferred site for oxygen activation and thereby protecting the Ni surface. In situ spectroscopy, transient and steady-state kinetics, and density functional theory calculations reveal the formation of a metastable C-Mo-O/Ni interface under reaction conditions. This interface provides a mechanism of O*-assisted C-H bond activation pathway instead of direct oxidation or combustion and reforming POM mechanism, lowering its activation energy. Concurrently, MoC x maintains Ni in electron-deficient metallic state, effectively suppressing its oxidation. It achieves ∼94% CH 4 conversion and 99% syngas selectivity during a 75-h stability test at 720 °C. This work underscores the role of transition metal carbides as functional oxygen regulators, where the formation of oxycarbide intermediates dictates catalytic performance. The philosophy for anti-oxidation stability could generate broader implications for heterogeneous catalyst design.

title: Unpacking the catastrophic cascade of the 2026 Gyirong disaster
Engineered E. coli Nissle 1917 alleviates colitis-associated depression via gut-brain axis restoration
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) patients disproportionately suffer from depression and anxiety, which exacerbate clinical outcomes yet remain inadequately addressed by current anti-tumor necrosis factor (TNF) biologics. To bridge this therapeutic gap, we engineered Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (eEcN) as a clinically translatable living microbial therapeutics platform for dual-targeted intervention. eEcN is designed to autonomously secrete immunomodulatory outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) bearing TNFα-neutralizing nanobodies (TNFαnb). These bioengineered nanovesicles specifically target inflamed colon tissue, enabling localized TNFα blockade, mucosal healing, and immune regulation. Concurrently, the eEcN remodels the gut microbiota, increasing symbiotic Lactobacillus abundance to elevate intestinal γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) levels, addressing a core neurotransmitter deficit in IBD-associated depression. In murine colitis models, this integrated strategy surpassed conventional anti-TNF therapy, simultaneously ameliorating intestinal pathology and depression-like behaviors. Mechanistically, eEcN attenuated neuroinflammation and restored hippocampal GABAergic neurotransmission via the gut-brain axis. This engineered living biomaterial platform, synergizing targeted OMVs-mediated nanobody delivery with microbiota-driven neurometabolite production, represents a promising approach for the complex pathophysiology of IBD and its neuropsychiatric comorbidities.

title: Coordination engineering enables highly selective generation of carbonate radicals for enhanced Fenton-like reactions
abstract: Abstract Overturning the conventional wisdom, recent studies demonstrated that bicarbonate ions (HCO) serve as promoters instead of inhibitors in heterogeneous Fenton-like processes. Nevertheless, the interfacial activation mechanisms of HCO and HO remain insufficiently understood, hindering the rational development of efficient catalytic processes. Herein, we report a coordination-regulated Co single-atom catalyst (SAC) that enables a highly selective pathway for carbonate radical (CO) generation. By constructing a six-coordinated CoN configuration (Co-N/C-T), the system achieved rapid and efficient degradation of sulfamethoxazole (SMX, 96.9%) within 60 min, with CO accounting for 98.9% of the total reactivity. Mechanistic insights from Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed the preferential adsorption and dissociation of peroxymonocarbonate (HCO) intermediate at CoN sites, facilitating selective generation of CO as the dominant reactive oxygen species (ROS). The Co-N/C-T Fenton-like system also exhibited robust performance and excellent recyclability at environmentally relevant concentrations across various realistic water matrices. Furthermore, a structure-reactivity correlation grounded in electronic descriptors revealed the system’s high selectivity toward electron-rich amine-containing antibiotics and their analogues, offering a targeted strategy for contaminant removal under complex water matrices. These findings provide mechanistic insights for advancing next-generation Fenton-like systems across diverse water treatment scenarios.

title: Nonreciprocal dynamic degeneracy splitting in non-Hermitian photonic crystals
abstract: Non-Hermitian dynamics offer promising ways to study the non-equilibrium phase of matter, such as chiral Zener tunneling, non-Bloch dynamics, and dynamic non-Hermitian skin effects, phenomena that cannot be fully captured by static eigenstate descriptions alone. Dynamic degeneracy splitting (DDS), which reveals the dynamic consequence caused by the uneven broadening of equal-frequency contours at a given excitation frequency, assists in investigating non-Hermitian dynamics. However, under reciprocity constraints, the theoretical and experimental studies of previous research on DDS have primarily focused on structures that exhibit centrosymmetric band structure and lifetime, leaving the distinctive phenomena associated with nonreciprocity largely unexplored. Here, we propose and realize nonreciprocal DDS through anisotropic damping of hyperbolic-like bands, induced by sequential symmetry breaking in a photonic crystal. This nonreciprocal DDS enables directional transmission via momentum-selective excitation in a stripe geometry and directional imaging in a slab geometry through anomalous negative refraction. These findings unify the concepts of nonreciprocity, non-Hermiticity, and dissipation anisotropy, demonstrating the opportunities enabled by artificial materials through symmetry engineering for tunable, highly directional wave propagation.

title: Enhancing interfacial stability of high-voltage LiCoO2 via fabricating a front-face with confined channels for desolvation
abstract: Lithium cobalt oxide (LiCoO 2 , LCO) is one of the most successful cathodes. However, it suffers from severe structural degradation and rapid capacity fading at high voltage (>4.5 V vs. Li + /Li). To improve high-voltage stability, researchers employ channel-type materials to desolvate lithium ions, resulting in a localized high-concentration environment. However, current channel-type materials, whether deployed as separators or additives, are hard to achieve effective desolvation of the electrolyte. Herein, we employ a facile and scalable high-speed solid-phase mechanofusion technique to construct a continuous and uniform zeolite coating layer on LCO (Zeolite@LCO). This inorganic zeolite layer physically decouples the Li + desolvation process from the electric-field-driven intercalation. Enabled by the complete Li + desolvation within the confined zeolite channels, a locally supersaturated electrolyte forms on the cathode surface, inherently suppressing the oxidative dehydrogenation of solvent molecules. Synergizing the confined channel effect with the intrinsic thermal robustness of the zeolite framework, this strategy comprehensively enhances the interfacial stability, thermal safety, and electrochemical performance of the Zeolite@LCO cathode. Consequently, Zeolite@LCO delivers an exceptional capacity retention of ∼83.0% after 300 cycles at a high cut-off voltage of 4.8 V. This confined channel interface design provides a highly translatable paradigm for developing high-energy-density cathodes innext-generation lithium-ion batteries.

title: From DNA packaging material to epigenetic information carrier: remembering the landmark 1996 histone studies in Tetrahymena
Programmable DNA–protein hydrogels: from structural DNA nanotechnology to adaptive soft matter
Impaired splicing of a conserved Pcyt2 minor intron in specific neuroglia contributes to spinal muscular atrophy
Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells and regenerative medicine
abstract: Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) continue to drive innovation in regenerative medicine, yet the field is undergoing a critical evolution from the early concept of cellular engraftment to complex paracrine-mediated tissue repair. This review systematically evaluates the core scientific questions defining this transition, highlighting the latest advancements in MSC biology and the rapidly expanding therapeutic frontier of MSC-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs). We critically appraise recent progress in decoding MSC therapeutic mechanisms, specifically their profound capacity for immune modulation and microenvironmental remodeling. By synthesizing current findings across diverse and challenging clinical applications-encompassing oral tissue regeneration, osteoarthritis, and complex immune disorders-we provide expert insights into the discrepancies between promising preclinical data and variable clinical outcomes. Crucially, we address persistent translational bottlenecks, including inherent donor heterogeneity, manufacturing scalability, and the lack of standardized potency assays. It is our perspective that overcoming these limitations demands a strategic pivot towards precise cell-free MSC-EV therapies and advanced bioengineering strategies. Ultimately, this review highlights key directions for future research. By connecting basic mechanistic insights with clinical demands, we aim to accelerate the translation of effective MSC-based therapies.

title: LEADO: unlocking functional insights from lipidomics data through mining lipid–gene–disease relationships
abstract: With the rapidly expanding repertoire of literature in the life sciences, efficiently extracting and integrating critical biomedical information from texts has emerged as an urgent challenge. Fuelled by the development of lipidomics, lipids have garnered increasing attention for their roles as essential molecules that regulate cellular signalling and metabolism, which underlie the pathogenesis of various diseases. Existing databases, however, primarily focus on genes, proteins, or small metabolite functions, with limited coverage of lipid-disease relationships, confining lipidomics application to a correlative framework. To address this gap, we developed Lipid Enrichment Analysis of Disease Ontology (LEADO), a BERT-based literature-mined knowledge database (https://lipidall-leado.com/leado/). We fine-tuned the BioBERT model to extract lipid entities and infer lipid-gene-disease associations, then constructed an interactive web platform using Shiny for data visualization and querying. LEADO serves as a comprehensive and user-friendly resource for exploring lipid-gene-disease relationships, with the potential to transform lipidomics toward a functional, causality-driven discipline that accelerates translational discovery in lipid metabolism.

title: A giant peanut-shaped ultra-high-energy γ-ray emitter off the galactic plane
abstract: Ultra-high-energy (UHE) gamma (γ) rays serve as unique probes for investigating new non-thermal astronomical phenomena within the Galaxy and also for studying PeV particle acceleration and propagation. Based on the UHE γ-ray survey conducted by LHAASO, this paper reports the discovery of a new source distinct from all previously identified high energy γ-ray objects. This source exhibits an elongated, peanut-like structure, which can be described as a rectangular strip measuring 4.6° in length and 0.45° in width, featuring two bright knots. It is located at a Galactic latitude of -17.5°, well below the Galactic plane and away from regions rich in UHE sources. The energy spectrum is spatially uniform across the entire region and is well fitted by a power-law model with an index of -1.95 and a cutoff at 250 TeV. The highest detected photon energy reaches 760 TeV. Morphological and spectral analyses indicate the presence of a powerful particle accelerator in this region, capable of accelerating particles beyond 1 PeV. An energetic millisecond pulsar (MSP) J0218 + 4232 is located at the brighter end of this source, with a spatial chance coincidence probability of 3.6 × 10 -4 , corresponding to 3.4σ. This suggests that the emission from this region very likely originates from particles accelerated within the MSP wind nebulae, potentially providing the first observational evidence supporting the wind nebulae of MSP as sources of UHE γ rays. However, the presence of other hidden accelerators, whether associated with known or entirely new populations of PeVatrons, cannot be ruled out, motivating future multi-wavelength observations.

title: Reimagining landslides: from geo-hazards to earth-surface system drivers
Active bacteria-delivered nanosystems for multimodal bladder cancer therapy
NoPro-clipping reveals a hidden universe of ubiquitinated glycogen and metabolites
Active regulation of synergistic interfacial materials for solar water purification
abstract: Coupling solar interfacial evaporation with photocatalysis provides a dual-functional strategy for simultaneous freshwater production and pollutant remediation. However, the current strategy of the passive stacking of functional layers faces bottlenecks due to inherent mechanistic conflicts, specifically manifested as the heat-adsorption paradox, mass transfer mismatch, and light energy competition, often resulting in a mutual loss of overall efficiency (1+1<2). To overcome these specific limitations, we propose a paradigm shift from passive assembly to active regulation. This review defines three core design principles aimed at precisely reconciling the aforementioned conflicts: (1) achieving spatial decoupling through a Janus structure, physically isolating the heat generation area from the exothermic adsorption sites to resolve thermodynamic conflicts; (2) implementing kinetic gating through a selective transport network, regulating reactant retention and preventing catalyst poisoning to address the mass transfer mismatch; (3) alleviating light energy competition through band synergy and energy modulation, and converting waste heat into catalytic potential. Furthermore, this article establishes a quantitative evaluation framework centered on the synergistic factor, aiming to accurately distinguish between physical volatilization and chemical mineralization, thereby eliminating efficiency illusions. Finally, this review outlines the path towards intelligent, closed-loop systems, emphasizing adaptive and self-regulating platforms for next-generation water purification.

title: Interfacial carbon vacancy stabilized ruthenium oxide for efficient acidic oxygen evolution
abstract: Advancement of proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) requires the development of high-performance catalysts for the anode acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER), particularly RuO x -based catalysts. However, practical applications have been hindered by poor stability, resulting from excessive oxygen leaching and severe RuO x agglomeration. Here, we report an interfacial carbon vacancy confined strategy to stabilize active RuO x nanoparticles on titanium carbide supports (TiC x ), delivering a mass activity of 1095.4 A g -1 Ru at 1.47 V vs. the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), outperforming most reported RuO x -based electrocatalysts, while maintaining stable operation over 600 h at 10 mA cm -2 . In-situ spectroscopic analyses, combined with theoretical calculations, reveal that the TiC x support reduces the overlap between Ru 4d and O 2p orbitals, thereby suppressing lattice oxygen reactivity and inhibiting the involvement of the detrimental lattice oxygen mechanism. Identical location transmission electron microscopy and molecular dynamics simulation demonstrate that carbon vacancies induce strong catalyst-support interactions, effectively maintaining well-dispersed RuO x nanoparticles without agglomeration during the OER. Importantly, the assembled PEMWE employing the as-prepared RuO x /TiC x catalyst achieves a low cell voltage of 1.61 V at 1 A cm -2 and high durability for over 200 h at 200 mA cm -2 . This interfacial vacancy confinement strategy provides an effective approach for designing highly durable electrocatalysts for practical applications.

title: A wearable accelerometry landscape of human health and disease
abstract: Digital wearable devices provide objective characterization of human behaviors in real-world settings, yet their implications for health and diseases remain incompletely understood. Here, we analyzed a large-scale accelerometry-based cohort, including 70,473 participants with up to 10 years of follow-up, yielding a total of 11.8 million person-hours of data. From this cohort, we constructed a comprehensive atlas of 210 accelerometer-derived phenotypes (ADPs), encompassing physical activity, sedentary behavior, sleep, circadian rhythm, step counts, and step intensity. The study identified 8149 ADP-disease and 36,614 ADP-trait associations across 406 diseases and 956 health-related traits. Step intensity and circadian rhythm emerged as the most prominent ADP domains associated with diseases. In addition, we developed an artificial intelligence (AI) framework, named Wearable-Accelerometry-based Temporal-Structural Network (WATSNet), achieving high discrimination (AUC >0.7) for 112 (28.1%) incident and 65 (34.0%) prevalent diseases, e.g., incidence of Parkinson's disease (AUC = 0.873) and dementia (AUC = 0.841). We provided evidence-informed behavioral benchmarks associated with lower disease risks: at least 0.8 h per day of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, 10,000 daily steps, and 7.8 h of sleep per day. Furthermore, we evaluated the generalizability of both ADP-disease associations and the performance of WATSNet in an external dataset (n = 4406). Together, these findings provide a comprehensive landscape linking digital behaviors to diverse health outcomes (https://digital-phenome-atlas.com) and a foundation for precision health monitoring.

title: T-linear specific heat in pressurized and magnetized Shastry-Sutherland Mott insulator SrCu2(BO3)2
abstract: The pressurized Shastry-Sutherland Mott insulator SrCu2(BO3)2 has been found to host a plaquette-singlet phase and an antiferromagnetic phase that break different symmetries spontaneously.The recent experiment showed that their transition is of a first order nature, which seems against the pursuit of exotic and deconfined degrees of freedom in this famous frustrated quantum magnet. We found a new direction in this study. By applying a magnetic field to the material, we discover that SrCu2(BO3)2 exhibits a universal and metallic T-linear specific heat behavior in a large magnetitic field range close to the pressure of zero-field first order transition between plaquette-singlet and antiferromagnetic phases. Such an unexpected gapless response from an electronically gapped Mott insulator could be attributed to magnetized Dirac spinons liberated by the combined effect of magnetic field and pressure, consistently seen from our quantum many-body thermal tensor network computation of the Shastry-Sutherland model under magnetic field. Such a robust and universal T-linear specific heat phase points out the richness of the phase diagram of the material expanded by the axes of pressure and magnetic field and is calling for new theoretical frameworks to its full explanation.

title: Measuring the jet-black hole spin misalignment in MAXI J1820 + 070
abstract: Abstract Compact relativistic jets are commonly observed across multiple wavelengths during the hard-state outbursts of black hole X-ray binaries. If the axis of the jet is misaligned with the black hole spin, the jet will precess due to the effect of frame dragging of the spinning black hole. In this work, we present the first measurement of this jet-spin misalignment by modeling the phase-resolved spectra of X-ray quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) detected in MAXI J1820+070 during its hard state. We find the misalignment angle to be $30.3\degree_{-3.1\degree}^{+3.2\degree}$, demonstrating significant evolution throughout the hard state, with the statistical significance much greater than $5\sigma$. This result supports a geometric origin for QPOs within the black hole spacetime and provides direct observational evidence that the low-frequency QPOs (LFQPOs) in MAXI J1820+070 arise from jet precession. The measured misalignment angle substantially exceeds the jet opening angle, suggesting that jet material undergoes stronger outward acceleration than predicted by current models.

title: Temporal metabolic-pool dynamics in ulcerative colitis remission
Ultrahigh-resolution photoluminescence visualization via triboelectrification effect
abstract: High-spatial-resolution visualization of localized physical stimuli remains constrained by structural and material limitations. Here, we develop a sub-micrometer-resolution visualization platform based on the nanoscale-triboelectrification-tuned photoluminescence (PL) in two-dimensional (2D) transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs). The PL intensity can be precisely regulated by controlling the contact force, scan rate and scan cycles of an atomic force microscopy (AFM) tip. With an AFM tip diameter of 20 nm and an excitation light wavelength of 532 nm, an ultrahigh resolution of 571.4 nm, corresponding to an equivalent pixel density of 44,452 pixels per inch, has been demonstrated, approaching the optical resolution limit. This work provides a proof-of-concept strategy for sub-micrometer-resolution PL visualization by coupling triboelectrification with the PL characteristic of 2D TMDCs. The proposed mechanism may provide a promising visualization platform for future high-resolution optical information encoding, mechanical mapping, and nano-optoelectronic systems.

title: Two-dimensional vermiculite neuroprotectants attenuate multifaceted complications in ischemic stroke
abstract: Multifaceted complications underlie suboptimal outcomes after ischemic stroke. Conventional single-target therapies fail to address the complex spatiotemporal evolution of these complications. In this work, we designed and engineered two-dimensional vermiculite nanosheets (VM NSs) as a neuroprotective platform that integrates surface-catalytic reactive oxygen species (ROS) neutralization with protein kinase B (AKT)-centered signaling modulation to mitigate ischemic-cascade complications across the full course of post-stroke pathology. VM NSs exert dual-action efficacy through a hierarchically organized catalysis-signaling axis: immediate surface-mediated redox reactions neutralize ROS, as supported by computational modeling. Concomitantly, stable hydrophobic interactions with the AKT pleckstrin homology domain modulate anti-inflammatory signaling, as revealed by molecular dynamics simulations and validated by increased AKT phosphorylation in microglia. These actions are synergistically coupled: initial ROS scavenging creates a favorable microenvironment that facilitates subsequent AKT-mediated anti-inflammatory and pro-repair effects, whereas anti-inflammatory signaling limits secondary ROS generation from activated microglia, establishing a positive feedback loop that amplifies neuroprotection. Multimodal imaging and histopathology confirm that cerebrospinal fluid-delivered VM NSs achieve ischemic-penumbra-specific biodistribution through microglial endocytosis, reducing infarction, restoring cerebral perfusion, preserving blood-brain barrier integrity, and preventing hemorrhagic transformation. This therapeutic platform addresses key translational limitations of monotherapies by combining computationally supported surface catalysis with protein-level signaling modulation, offering an interdisciplinary paradigm for managing post-stroke complications throughout disease progression.

title: Individualized exercise for body recomposition and multidimensional health in type 2 diabetes
TGW1a breaks the trade-off between early maturity and high yield for intensive rice cropping
Finite-time thermodynamics unveils barriers in photocatalysis
81Kr evidence for Late Pleistocene ice preservation in the Guliya Ice Cap, Tibetan Plateau
Spatial confinement-modulated photoluminescence in two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks
First determination of the full spin density matrix in ψ(3686)→ΛΛ¯
abstract: Using (448.1±2.9)×10 6 ψ(3686) events collected with the BESIII detector, we present the first complete determination of the spin density matrix in ψ(3686)→ΛΛ¯. This provides a unified framework to study both the production dynamics and the quantum correlations of the ΛΛ¯ system. From a five-dimensional joint angular analysis, we determine α ψ =0.82±0.02 stat. ±0.01 syst. and ΔΦ=20.6±3.6 stat. ±0.6 syst. °. The non-zero phase implies a transverse polarization of Λ, with a maximum value of P y =0.074±0.013 stat. ±0.003 syst. and a significance of 6.3σ. The same framework also gives access to the spin correlations of the baryon pair and enables tests of quantum nonclassicality. The average of the Bell nonlocality measure is determined to be m¯ 12 =1.266±0.078 stat. ±0.049 syst. , yielding a violation of the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt inequality with a significance of 3.7σ. These results establish ψ(3686)→ΛΛ¯ as a unique laboratory for unified studies of hadron production dynamics and quantum entanglement in a system of massive baryons.

title: Site-specific self-protection of stacking faults enables durable Li–gas batteries
abstract: Rechargeable Li-gas batteries, represented by Li-O 2 and Li-CO 2 systems, are promising for high-energy-density storage and gas-involved energy conversion, yet their operation is constrained by the trade-off between catalytic activity and structural durability of cathodes. Metastable defects such as stacking faults offer active sites for accelerating sluggish gas redox reactions, but readily undergo electrochemical stress-induced slip and structural collapse during cycling. Inspired by plant traumatic resinosis, we propose a site-specific self-protection strategy that exploits the intrinsic anisotropy of stacking faults to decouple catalytic reaction planes from orthogonal protective functional planes. On the reaction plane, over-coordinated dislocation sites amplify surface electrostatic potential differences and promote Li 2 CO 3 decomposition via nucleophilic/electrophilic interactions. On the functional plane, selective interactions with sulfur-containing electrolyte components induce in situ reconstruction of a multiphase inorganic-organic amorphous interphase, anchoring stacking faults without blocking catalytic sites. As a Li-CO 2 proof of concept, stacking-fault-rich molybdenum boride (MoB) delivers 90.13% average energy efficiency over 2500 h and stable operation at 150 °C for nearly 500 h. This work establishes a self-protection paradigm for stable metastable active structures and provides a universal interface design principle for durable Li-gas batteries.

title: Mechanically robust solid electrolyte interphase via in situ adhesion of organic–inorganic bilayers for energy-dense lithium metal batteries
abstract: The poor mechanical stability of solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) critically compromises the cycle life of practical lithium (Li) metal batteries, as repeated volume changes induce continuous SEI fracture and regeneration. Here, we propose a robust organic layer, in situ formed from 3‑glycidoxypropyltrimethoxysilane (GPTS) and anchored onto an inorganic underlayer, to enhance interfacial adhesion between the organic and inorganic layer, thereby improving the mechanical stability of the SEI. The epoxy groups of GPTS can polymerize in situ to form a robust organic layer, while the methoxysilane groups facilitate the anchoring of the organic layer onto the inorganic layer through chemical reactions. The elastic modulus of the formed bilayer SEI is much enhanced, thereby effectively mitigating its cracking and reconstruction during cycles. Li metal coin cells with GPTS-derived SEI deliver capacity retention of 80% after 290 cycles under practical conditions, which is 1.6 times higher than that of the coin cells with base SEI. A 5.5 Ah Li metal pouch cell with GPTS-derived SEI achieves a high energy density of 503 Wh kg -1 and maintains stable cycling for 107 cycles. This work presents a rational strategy for engineering the SEI nanostructure to enhance mechanical stability, thereby promoting the stability of Li metal anodes.

title: CRISPR-backpacked macrophages for immune activation against bone metastasis
Large language model-guided high-throughput screening for accelerated discovery of Pt-based high-entropy electrocatalysts
abstract: Pt-based high-entropy alloy (Pt-HEA) catalysts show significant potential for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet their vast compositional space challenges conventional trial-and-error approaches. Here, we propose a large language model (LLM)-guided closed-loop framework for high-throughput discovery to accelerate the rational design and optimization of Pt-HEA catalysts. The framework first extracts structured knowledge from extensive literature and incorporates retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to develop an LLM assistant tailored to HEA electrocatalysis research. The assistant transforms scattered literature knowledge, experimental constraints, and platform capabilities into experimentally feasible Pt-HEA candidate combinations and executable experimental protocols. High-throughput synthesis and screening enabled rapid evaluation of multiple Pt-HEA candidates, followed by Bayesian optimization to efficiently refine compositions within the representative Fe-Co-Ni-Cu-Pt system. This established a collaborative closed-loop workflow linking LLM-assisted candidate generation, high-throughput feedback, Bayesian optimization recommendations, density functional theory (DFT) mechanistic interpretation, and proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) device validation. Using this framework, we completed three iterative cycles involving 50 samples within 48 h, revealing how HER activity depends on atomic ratios in the Fe-Co-Ni-Cu-Pt system and identifying Fe 30 Co 30 Ni 10 Cu 10 Pt 20 as the optimal composition. Theoretical calculations demonstrated that the multimetallic local coordination environment formed by Fe, Co, Ni, and Cu regulates the electronic structure of Pt active sites and fine-tunes the Pt-H interaction. Further PEMWE testing confirmed the catalyst’s promising performance under device operating conditions. This work establishes a generalizable closed-loop paradigm integrating literature knowledge, experimental feedback, and model-driven decision-making, offering a viable route to the rational design and efficient optimization of complex multicomponent electrocatalytic materials.

title: Emerging ultraviolet mechanoluminescent materials: mechanisms, design, and advanced applications
abstract: Mechanoluminescent (ML) materials directly convert mechanical energy into light, enabling applications in intelligent stress sensing and advanced light sources. Ultraviolet (UV) ML materials, particularly those operating in the solar-blind region (200-280 nm), offer significant advantages for high-signal-to-noise-ratio outdoor sensing owing to minimal interference from sunlight filtered by the Earth's ozone layer. Recent studies have demonstrated that rare-earth ions (Ce 3+ , Pr 3+ , Gd 3+ , Tm 3+ , Er 3+ , and Tb 3+ ) and Bi 3+ ions facilitate tunable ML emissions across the UVA to UVC spectral range. Advanced material design strategies such as trap-state modulation, piezo-/tribo-electric coupling, and molecular crystal engineering have been used to develop high-performance UV ML materials with enhanced ML intensity and tunable emission wavelengths. Despite these advances, a comprehensive systematic review focusing specifically on UV ML materials is lacking. This review addresses this critical gap by providing an in-depth analysis of the fundamental mechanisms, rational design principles, and performance optimization strategies for UV ML materials. Furthermore, this paper critically summarizes emerging applications in anti-counterfeiting, environmental sensing, structural monitoring, and UV disinfection. By identifying the current challenges and future research directions, this study aims to serve as a foundational reference for accelerating the development and practical implementation of next-generation UV ML materials.

title: Taming inflammation in coronary artery disease: lessons learned, translational breakthroughs, and future directions
abstract: Inflammation is an essential physiological process that preserves host homeostasis, yet chronic inflammation is now recognized as a common pathological basis of many diseases. In coronary artery disease (CAD), chronic inflammation is central to the initiation and progression of atherosclerosis. Accordingly, anti-inflammatory therapy has emerged as a major focus of investigation in this field. Although multiple inflammatory pathways have been evaluated as therapeutic targets in clinical trials, strategies with demonstrated clinical benefit remain limited. In this review, we examine the sources of inflammation in CAD, approaches to inflammatory risk stratification, and advances in anti-inflammatory therapy. To explain divergent trial outcomes and guide future clinical translation, we propose a 4R framework: the right target, the right patient, the right timing, and the right benefit-risk balance. Anti-inflammatory treatment remains promising. Within this framework, refined inflammatory phenotyping and evaluation of stage-dependent efficacy represent immediate priorities for future trials.

title: High-initial-efficiency sodium storage in crystalline carbon nitride mediated by quasi-metallic Zn-N4 sites for wide-temperature batteries
Structural insights and engineering of deep-sea halophilic PET hydrolytic enzymes
Dynamic proton reservoir with hydrogen-bond-network-mediated proton transport pathway for efficient alkaline hydrogen evolution
abstract: The alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is intrinsically limited by the lack of active hydrogen and sluggish hydrogen transfer. However, current strategies mainly optimize catalytic sites for water splitting or hydrogen adsorption, overlooking the demands of continuous hydrogen supply and rapid hydrogen transfer. Here, we report an IrO 2 /WO 3 catalyst that enables dynamic engineering of proton reservoirs and transport pathways for accelerated alkaline HER. The catalyst exhibits exceptional alkaline HER activity, delivering an ultralow overpotential of 18 mV at 10 mA cm -2 for alkaline HER. When integrated into a membrane-based alkaline electrolyzer, it achieves 1 A cm -2 at only 1.68 V and retains stable performance for over 1000 h. Experimental and theoretical studies show that WO 3 undergoes reversible proton intercalation and deintercalation, acting as a dynamic proton reservoir. More importantly, the strong interfacial coupling between IrO 2 and WO 3 reconstructs an ordered hydrogen-bond network that serves as an efficient proton transport pathway and facilitates directional proton transfer to Ir active sites. Meanwhile, IrO 2 efficiently stabilizes H* intermediates, thereby accelerating H-H coupling. This work reveals the critical role of dynamic proton microenvironments in governing alkaline HER kinetics, providing a new strategy for proton-coupled electrocatalyst design.

title: A printable meta-assembly strategy for scalable structural coloration
Toward 700 Wh kg−1 lithium-metal batteries using lithium-rich manganese-based oxides: realistic strategies and perspective
Megalin-targeted Mg–Fe cyanometallate framework nanozymes calibrate mitochondrial iron–calcium homeostasis to treat acute kidney injury
abstract: Intracellular metal ion homeostasis, particularly the precise regulation of mitochondrial iron and calcium, is essential for maintaining energy metabolism and cell survival. Once disrupted, iron-mediated oxidative reactions and calcium overload mutually amplify, rapidly leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and cellular injury. In acute kidney injury (AKI), this mitochondria-centered iron-calcium imbalance represents a critical pathological axis driving oxidative stress, programmed cell death, and inflammation. However, effective therapies that coordinately regulate both processes are not yet available. Herein, we developed a polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP)-coated Mg-Fe cyanometallate framework nanozyme (MFC) to calibrate iron-calcium homeostasis in AKI. The PVP coating facilitates its interaction with the highly expressed Megalin receptor in renal proximal tubular epithelial cells, promoting receptor-dependent endocytosis and tubular-targeted delivery. Built on a Prussian blue-like coordination framework, MFC efficiently captures bioactive iron to suppress oxidative stress, while its ion-exchange process concurrently releases Mg 2+ , acting as a physiological calcium antagonist that regulates mitochondrial calcium homeostasis. By stabilizing mitochondrial structure and function, this strategy suppresses the cascade amplification of cell death and inflammatory signaling, significantly ameliorating renal injury in AKI. This study proposes a therapeutic approach for AKI by rewiring mitochondrial iron-calcium imbalance and offers a design paradigm for multifactorially coupled diseases.

title: Identifying priorities for advancing SDGs in Africa
abstract: Africa faces enormous challenges in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), with only 6% of measurable targets currently on track. Identifying priorities is a fundamental prerequisite for achieving the SDGs. Here, we compiled a comprehensive time-series database covering SDG indicators for 41 African countries. By integrating network analysis with Granger causality analysis, we identified the most influential SDGs across the continent. We found that Africa's progress toward the SDGs has slowed since the adoption of the 2030 Agenda. Prioritizing SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure) generated the strongest positive spillover effects across the SDG network. Countries with relatively low performance on SDG 9 and stronger governance capacity derived greater benefits from advancing this goal. These findings suggest that, for most African countries, prioritizing the advancement of SDG 9 yields the highest returns for overall SDG progress. This study not only provides evidence-based guidance for accelerating Africa's progress toward the SDGs but also offers a valuable reference point for other regions facing comparable development challenges.

title: Genomic evidence resolves diversification and fossil taxonomic ambiguities of endangered East Asian gazelles
abstract: Procapra (East Asian gazelles) is a genus of antelopes endemic to Asia, with three extant species inhabiting both plateau and steppe regions. Previous morphological and limited molecular studies suggested that the uplift of the Tibetan Plateau during the Pleistocene may have driven diversification within this genus. However, due to the lack of comprehensive whole-genomic data, the details of diversification and phylogenetic structure within this genus remain unresolved. In this study, we sequenced whole genomes of both ancient and modern Procapra individuals to explore their evolutionary history and genetic diversity. Our results identified two major divergence events: the first, around 0.5 Ma, leading to the divergence of Tibetan gazelle (Procapra picticaudata, Tib), and the second, around 0.12 Ma, resulting in the separation between Mongolian gazelle (Procapra gutturosa, Mon) and Przewalski's gazelle (Procapra przewalskii, Prz). We also detected post-divergence gene flow among species, which complicated their phylogenetic relationships. This is especially true for the shallow divergence between Prz and Mon in contrast to their current taxonomic separation. Furthermore, demographic analyses revealed that population contractions were possibly linked to climate changes and human impacts. Additionally, ancient DNA analyses suggested that several Late Pleistocene specimens from northeastern China, previously attributed to Prz, are more closely related to Mon. These findings underscore the importance of integrating genomic data when recognizing ancient specimens' identity and evolutionary relationships in Procapra, particularly in the context of shallow divergence and historical gene flow.

title: Enhanced piezoelectricity and nanotopography resolve the infection-regeneration conflict in implant-associated osteomyelitis
abstract: Implant-associated osteomyelitis remains a major clinical challenge because antibacterial therapy and bone regeneration impose competing demands within a dysregulated osteoimmune microenvironment. Strategies targeting antibacterial activity or osteogenesis alone are insufficient to address these interlinked challenges. Here, we develop a microenvironment-responsive interface composed of poly(L-lactic acid) (PLLA) and zinc oxide (ZnO) that integrates enhanced piezoelectricity with engineered nanotopography to support bone repair. Surface-exposed ZnO nanowire arrays markedly enhance the piezoelectric output of the PLLA interface and enable pH-responsive Zn 2+ release. This synergistic design enables on-demand activation under infection-associated acidic conditions, while the nanowire topography provides potent antibacterial activity through mechanical penetration, thereby addressing the infection-regeneration conflict. The interface thereby enables spatiotemporally coordinated antibacterial, immunomodulatory, and osteogenic responses, reshaping the osteoimmune microenvironment. In vitro, the interface exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, promotes macrophage polarization toward a pro-healing phenotype, and enhances the osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells. In a rat model of implant-associated osteomyelitis, the interface significantly suppresses bacterial colonization, attenuates inflammatory responses, and promotes bone regeneration and osseointegration, achieving a 3-fold higher bone volume/tissue volume ratio than uncoated controls while maintaining favorable biosafety. Collectively, this work establishes a microenvironment-adaptive interface that integrates antibacterial and bone-regenerative functions, offering a promising strategy for treating implant-associated osteomyelitis.

title: Mechanistic state-space mapping of degradation in perovskite solar cells
A lncCtxnd1-encoded micropeptide suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma by reprogramming tumor-associated macrophages
Plant histone variants: deposition mechanisms, functional diversification, and translational prospects
abstract: Histone variants are non-allelic isoforms of canonical histones that assemble into nucleosomes via replication-independent pathways, reshaping chromatin biophysical properties and transcriptional control at specific genomic loci. Constrained by their sessile lifestyle, plants have evolved a rich set of histone variants, including lineage-specific innovations such as heterochromatin-stabilizing H2A.W, stress-inducible H1.3, gametophyte-restricted H2B.8, Arabidopsis H3.14, and Oryza-specific H4.V. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in plant histone variants from three dimensions: (1) histone chaperones and remodelers governing variant genomic targeting; (2) variant functions across plant developmental and stress responses; (3) evolutionary origins and epigenetic crosstalk underlying variant diversification. Comparative and pan-genomic analyses reveal that lineage-specific gene-family expansion and intraspecific structural variation jointly shape plant histone variant repertoires. Natural histone variant haplotypes provide untapped genetic resources for fine-tuning chromatin responsiveness, though their causal links to chromatin states and agronomic traits remain to be experimentally validated. We propose the concept of pangenomic chromatin alleles, in which naturally occurring histone-variant haplotypes, copy-number variations, and structural configurations at histone-variant loci may be leveraged to fine-tune chromatin responsiveness and inform future pan-genome-based chromatin haplotype breeding. We further discuss how crop pangenomes, multi-modal artificial intelligence, and precision epigenome editing can accelerate variant discovery, occupancy prediction, and functional prioritization, while emphasizing the necessity of rigorous genetic and biochemical validation for all predictive findings.

title: Agri-food connectivity drives the resurgence and geographic expansion of human brucellosis in China
abstract: Agri-food systems are increasingly recognised as drivers of zoonotic disease emergence, yet the mechanisms by which modern food production, trade, and distribution reshape pathogen transmission remain poorly quantified. Here we integrate two decades of nationwide surveillance, epidemiological modelling, and phylogenomic analyses of 4215 Brucella genomes from 79 countries and regions to elucidate the drivers of brucellosis re-emergence in China. Nationwide, human cases increased by 282.6% between 2005 and 2023, far exceeding the 8.1% increase in sheep inventory. This decoupling indicates a fundamental shift in transmission pathways. In northern China, livestock reservoir and production indicators accounted for 88.9% of the relative model contribution, consistent with direct occupational exposure; whereas in southern China, the agri-food logistics and market connectivity domain showed the largest contribution (64.1%), providing quantitative evidence that modern food-distribution infrastructure now drives brucellosis risk in those regions. Demographic shifts reaffirm this transition, with marked incidence increases among children and the elderly, indicating expanded foodborne and household exposures. Phylogenomics reveals that China's epidemic reflects long-term endemic amplification of a dominant Brucella melitensis clade (Lineage 2.4), with a hierarchical hub-and-spoke transmission network linking northern pastoral source regions to historically non-endemic southern provinces through national livestock and logistics networks. Comparative genomics further identifies lineage-specific gene acquisitions, adaptive variation in the outer membrane protein Omp2b, and recurrent convergent disruption of puuD enriched among winter isolates. Together, these findings reframe brucellosis resurgence as an emergent property of agri-food connectivity and highlight domestic supply chains, transport hubs, and cold-chain infrastructure as priority targets for surveillance and intervent ion.

title: Dual-effect confinement engineering reconciles electromagnetic wave absorption with marine corrosion protection
abstract: The simultaneous achievement of efficient electromagnetic wave absorption (EWA) and long-term corrosion protection in complex marine environments remains challenging due to inherent structural conflicts between porous electromagnetic absorbers and compact anticorrosion coatings. Herein, a multi-scale spatial assembly strategy is proposed to construct a three-dimensional hollow spherical carbon foam (HSCF) decorated with layered double hydroxide (LDH) nanosheets via a three-stage process (protonation, morphological reconstruction, and confined assembly) to realize a dual-effect confinement mechanism. From the perspective of electromagnetic energy confinement, enhanced synergistic effects among the architectural units induce intensive scattering and polarization loss, achieving a minimum reflection loss of -68.11 dB and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 7.40 GHz. Electromagnetic simulations further confirm the outstanding radar stealth capabilities across a wide range of incident angles. From the perspective of corrosive media confinement, the tortuous HSCF skeleton physically retards the diffusion of corrosive species, while the anchored LDH nanosheets actively capture chloride ions via anion exchange. Consequently, the resulting HSCF@LDH/epoxy (EP) composite coating exhibits excellent corrosion resistance, featuring a significantly enhanced corrosion potential and reduced current density compared with the pure EP coating. Overall, this dual-effect confinement mechanism enabled by the multi-scale spatial assembly strategy establishes a new structural paradigm for the next generation of multifunctional EWA materials for extreme operational environments.

title: Gut-associated germinal center-like structures in teleosts reveal early origin of mucosal adaptive immunity
Charting brain growth in Chinese children with Autism
Environmental governance transition shaped China’s five-decade water pollutant reduction
abstract: China has experienced a complex decoupling of water pollutant discharges from economic growth, shaped by a range of environmental governance interventions. However, the intervention mechanisms underlying long-term pollutant reductions remain insufficiently quantified. We proposed a long-term annual estimation model for estimating Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) and Ammonia Nitrogen (NH 3 -N) discharges that incorporates logistic change simulation, Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) decomposition, and text-mining-based quantification of mandatory policy intensity to represent time-varying environmental governance. We estimated annual pollutant discharges for all prefecture-level divisions in China from 1970 to 2100 and disentangled the contributions of multiple governance measures across the generation–governance–discharge chain. Results show that pollutant discharges exceed the safe boundary in the 1990s, peak in 2006, and subsequently decline by 20%–40% by 2020. This trajectory reflects a staged governance transition from limited governance to generation control and then to end-of-pipe treatment, with respective contributions of 0.0%–2.6%, 6.1%–21.3%, and 17.2%–50.8%. This transition is accompanied by marked spatial heterogeneity. Coastal regions achieve decoupling primarily through end-of-pipe treatment (55.3% and 62.9% of COD and NH 3 -N reductions, respectively), whereas the northwestern region relies more heavily on generation control (46.9% and 28.8%, respectively). Future COD reductions are projected to be increasingly constrained by livestock-related discharges, whereas NH 3 -N discharges are projected to fall below the safe boundary around 2035, driven by continued improvements in wastewater infrastructure. Our findings reveal distinct stages in China’s environmental governance transition and provide insights for water environmental management in China and other late-industrializing countries.

title: China’s new PM2.5 standards may shift the paradigm of air pollution control
Spatiotemporal mapping reveals microbiota-dependent maintenance of functional competence during postnatal immune maturation
abstract: Postnatal immune maturation is commonly viewed as a developmental milestone associated with weaning. However, how postnatal microbiota exposure shapes immune cell heterogeneity across tissues, and whether this maturation is self-sustaining or requires continuous microbial input, remain unclear. Here, we conducted spatiotemporal single-cell transcriptomic profiling of 120,649 immune cells isolated from 10 tissues in both germ-free (GF) and specific pathogen-free (SPF) mice from weaning to adulthood. We demonstrate that microbial colonization drives the expansion and functional maturation of distinct monocyte, macrophage, and neutrophil populations, marked by enhanced antigen-processing capabilities across tissues. Simultaneously, commensal-derived signals reprogram lymphocyte metabolic and translational states, promoting oxidative phosphorylation and relieving PDCD4-mediated translational repression to sustain effector readiness. Notably, microbiota reconstitution through both co-housing and fecal microbiota transplantation demonstrated that immune competence is not a fixed developmental endpoint but instead requires continuous microbiota-derived input. Without sustained microbial signals, immune cells adopted a persistent hyporesponsive state rather than remaining developmentally immature. Together, these findings redefine immune maturation as a microbiota-dependent maintenance process, revealing potential strategies to restore immune competence through microbiota-targeted interventions.

title: Donor-derived unlicensed NK cells promote the hematopoietic engraftment and survival after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
abstract: Successful hematopoietic engraftment is critical for the prognosis of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), as delayed or failed engraftment remains a major cause of transplant failure. Natural killer (NK) cells, particularly recipient-derived unlicensed NK (U-NK) cells, have been reported to promote hematopoietic recovery under non-myeloablative conditioning (non-MAC). However, following myeloablative conditioning (MAC), recipient-derived NK cells are largely depleted, highlighting the need to investigate the role of donor-derived NK cells. In this study, we analyzed a clinical cohort of 976 patients who underwent haploidentical HSCT following MAC and validated our findings in both the original and propensity score-matched cohorts. Our results demonstrated that the presence of donor-derived U-NK cells was associated with faster hematopoietic recovery and improved outcomes, including reduced treatment-related mortality (TRM) and superior long-term survival. Notably, these effects were independent of recipient human leukocyte antigen (HLA) typing. Multivariate analyses further identified donor U-NK status as an independent protective factor for hematopoietic engraftment, TRM, and overall survival. Mechanistically, U-NK cells directly enhanced hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell colony formation in vitro, both independently and through stromal cell interactions. In vivo, infusion of U-NK cells markedly accelerated neutrophil and platelet engraftment. This was accompanied by increased granulocyte-monocyte progenitors, megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitors and multipotent progenitors early post-transplant, along with elevated plasma levels of FVII and serum amyloid A1 (SAA1). Collectively, donor-derived U-NK cells promote hematopoietic engraftment and improve transplant outcomes independently of recipient HLA typing, supporting their potential as a donor selection biomarker and providing a therapeutic strategy for addressing engraftment failure.

title: Associations of body shape, visceral adiposity, and metabolic function indices with risk of major noncommunicable diseases: evidence from a nationwide population cohort
abstract: Comparative data evaluating the predictive performance of various obesity and metabolic indices for multiple noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) remain limited. We used the data sourced from the Health Evaluation and risk Reduction through nationwide Teamwork cohort (ChinaHEART), a national population-based study that enrolled 4,258,033 Chinese adults and followed them for more than 20 million person-years between November 2014 and December 2023. Fifteen obesity and metabolic indices were categorized into three groups: (1) body shape-related indices, including body mass index (BMI), body roundness index (BRI), waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), a body shape index (ABSI), weight-adjusted waist index (WWI), and conicity index (CI); (2) visceral fat-related indices, including lipid accumulation product (LAP) and Chinese visceral adiposity index (CVAI); and (3) metabolic function-related indices, including triglyceride-glucose index (TyG), TyG-BMI, TyG-BRI, TyG-WHtR, TyG-ABSI, TyG-WWI, and TyG-CI. The study outcomes comprised composite events of death or first hospitalization attributable to each of cardiovascular diseases (CVD), diabetes mellitus (DM), cancers, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) individually. Composite obesity and metabolic indices reflecting visceral adiposity accumulation and insulin resistance, respectively exhibited enhanced predictive accuracy for cardiovascular and diabetic risk, whereas their performance for cancer and COPD was comparatively limited. These findings support the paradigm that weight management strategies should be guided by risk assessments rather than relying solely on body weight or body shape. Furthermore, the development of diverse definitions for obesity measurement and management tailored to different population subgroups is warranted.

title: Electric-field-responsive solvation: stabilizing high-voltage lithium metal batteries through adaptive interfacial chemistry
Molecular filler-enhanced DNA nanomachines enable one-step multiplex quantification of ctDNA for mutation analysis and metastasis-associated assessment
abstract: Detection of low-abundance biomarkers like circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) remains challenging for molecular diagnosis and therapeutic management of cancer. Here, we developed a homogeneous electrochemical platform using metal ion-mediated DNA self-assembly enhanced by molecular fillers, enabling simultaneous, amplification-free, label-free, and enzyme-free detection of dual biomarkers. Incorporation of methylene blue into DNA nanostructures can suppress non-specific ion leakage, enhance sensitivity by 100-fold and signal-to-noise ratio by 2.5-fold. Target binding triggered DNA nanomachines disassembly, releasing Ag + or Hg 2+ for simultaneously electrochemical analysis, thereby facilitating precise quantification of the target biomarkers. The system achieved high-performance detection of L858R and T790M with limits of 5.2 and 6.0 amol/L, respectively, when applied to epidermal growth factor receptor mutations in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Using qPCR as the reference, mutation detection achieved AUCs of 0.96 for both L858R and T790M. In disease discrimination, L858R showed moderate sensitivity, whereas T790M provided limited discrimination in the predominantly treatment-naive cohort. In addition, the platform also demonstrated applicability in detecting BRAF V600E mutations in thyroid cancer. Exploratory analyses further revealed differences in ctDNA-associated signals between non-metastatic and metastatic cases. This filler-enhanced DNA nanomachine strategy offered a high-performance tool for ultrasensitive ctDNA analysis and showed potential for clinical applications.

title: Self-reinforcing immunometabolic microneedles enable circuit-level lactate reprogramming to enhance solid tumor immunotherapy
abstract: Excessive lactate accumulation in solid tumors disrupts metabolic-immune coordination within the tumor microenvironment, driving acidosis, immune suppression, and resistance to immunotherapy. Current lactate-targeting strategies mainly act on isolated metabolic nodes and therefore fail to restore coordinated control over lactate production, intracellular utilization, and extracellular immunosuppression. Here, we develop a self-reinforcing immunometabolic microneedle platform (LZH/PC MNs) to reconstruct the tumor lactate regulatory circuit at multiple levels. Calcium carbonate-mineralized photosynthetic cyanobacteria and lactate oxidase-loaded zeolitic imidazolate framework nanoparticles (LZH NPs) are hierarchically integrated into dissolvable microneedles for localized intratumoral delivery. In the acidic tumor microenvironment, calcium carbonate consumes protons to alleviate extracellular acidosis while replenishing calcium ions. Following cellular internalization, LZH NPs catalyze intracellular lactate oxidation to generate oxidative stress, thereby sustaining calcium overload and inducing immunogenic cell death. Meanwhile, light-driven photosynthetic oxygenation enhances lactate oxidase activity, destabilizes hypoxia-inducible factor 1α, suppresses glycolysis-driven lactate production, and promotes macrophage repolarization. Through the integrated regulation of extracellular acidosis alleviation, intracellular lactate depletion, and upstream metabolic inhibition, LZH/PC MNs restore lactate homeostasis, rewire tumor metabolic-immune crosstalk, and elicit systemic antitumor immunity against both primary and distant tumors. This work establishes tumor lactate metabolism as a circuit-level immunometabolic target and provides a generalizable strategy for overcoming lactate-driven immune resistance in solid tumors.

title: Gut microbiota-derived UDP-GlcNAc co-opts the host O-GlcNAcylation system to fuel breast tumour progression
abstract: The gut microbiome is increasingly linked to breast cancer (BC) progression; however, specific microbial metabolites and their direct mechanistic connections to oncogenic signalling remain poorly defined. Here, using multi-omics analyses in treatment-naïve patients with BC, we identified gut microbiota-derived uridine diphosphate N-acetylglucosamine (UDP-GlcNAc) as a circulating oncometabolite associated with therapeutic response. We further showed that Ruminococcus lactaris is a key intestinal commensal capable of de novo UDP-GlcNAc biosynthesis, and that microbial-derived UDP-GlcNAc acts as an independent tumour-promoting metabolite, even though the host hexosamine pathways generate the majority of circulating UDP-GlcNAc pools. Mechanistically, UDP-GlcNAc systemically activates O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT), stabilizing the transcription factor NFIB, and triggers a feed-forward loop that upregulates OGT and the proto-oncogene KIT, thereby driving BC progression. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of OGT disrupts this signaling axis and suppresses tumour growth, even in the presence of UDP-GlcNAc-producing bacteria. These findings reveal a gut microbiota-metabolite-host signalling circuit, in which a microbial metabolite hijacks a core host post-translational modification pathway to promote BC progression, providing novel opportunities for microbiome-targeted diagnosis and therapy.

title: Electron delocalization orchestrated Zn2+ reduction chemistry enables highly reversible Zn metal anodes
abstract: Aqueous Zn metal batteries are limited by sluggish Zn 2+ reduction kinetics and interfacial instability, while the mechanistic role of alcohol-based additives remains unclear. Here, we establish an electron delocalization orchestrated Zn 2+ reduction chemistry using cyclic polyols with identical carbon numbers and functional group quantity but distinct topologies, including inositol, mannitol, and sorbitol. We show that electron delocalization across hydroxyl donor sites governs their effective utilization, thereby coupling Zn 2+ solvation structure reconstruction with interfacial electrostatics regulation of the anodes. Among these, inositol exhibits a highly delocalized electronic structure and uniform charge distribution, which maximizes hydroxyl groups participation in Zn 2+ coordination and hydrogen bond rearrangement. This coordinated environment lowers local charge density around Zn 2+ , accelerates charge transfer, and homogenizes the interfacial electric field, collectively promoting rapid and uniform Zn deposition. As a result, Zn||Zn cells sustain stable cycling for over 2700 h under harsh conditions, and Zn||Zn x V 2 O 5 ·nH 2 O full cells deliver prolonged cycling stability. This work identifies electron delocalization as a molecular descriptor that governs Zn 2+ reduction chemistry and establishes a general framework for designing highly reversible Zn metal anodes.

title: MST4 kinase maintains B cell survival and function by phosphorylating PRDX1 during inflammation
Visualization of anomalous electromechanical coupling at atomic scale
abstract: Piezoelectric materials enable the direct interconversion of mechanical and electrical energy and are therefore widely used in stress sensors, wearable devices, and information-storage technologies. Controllably modulating piezoelectric coefficients could significantly enhance piezoelectric responses and thereby improve device performance. Sliding ferroelectrics in two-dimensional van der Waals materials offer opportunities to regulate piezoelectricity through stacking manipulation. Here, using atomic-scale in situ biasing high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy, we directly visualized electric-field-induced interlayer sliding and intralayer atomic displacements in γ-InSe under different bias voltages and correlated the structural evolution with a field-dependent, nonmonotonic polarity reversal in the transverse electromechanical response, revealing anomalous electromechanical coupling in γ-InSe. Together with theoretical calculations, these observations attribute the anomalous piezoelectric behavior to competition between clamped-ion and internal-strain contributions induced by concurrent changes in interlayer stacking configuration and intralayer atomic displacement. These findings provide insights into the ferroelectric mechanism of γ-InSe and suggest routes for tuning piezoelectric coefficients in sliding ferroelectrics, thereby informing the design of next-generation piezoelectric and electromechanical devices.

title: Oxygen-mediated Lewis acid sites in polymeric carbon nitride for H2O2 photosynthesis
abstract: Photocatalysis for hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) photosynthesis, believed to be an alternative to the conventional anthraquinone method, has yet to overcome the sluggish proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process and unsatisfactory photocatalytic activity. Herein, an O-mediated Lewis acid site regulation strategy was proposed for polymeric carbon nitride (CN) with alkali metals (MA: Na, K, Rb, Cs) doped into the molecular structure. The alkali metals doped into the CN framework, particularly Cs, acting as strong electron donors, would significantly delocalize the π system in the CN framework for improved charge transfer ability, as well as induce strong electronic polarization across the O-mediated electronic bridge to generate electron-deficient O-adjacent C centers with enhanced Lewis acidity for molecular O 2 activation. Accordingly, Cs-OCN exhibits the smallest reaction free-energy change for the thermodynamically demanding *OOH → *H 2 O 2 step, thereby favoring PCET-mediated H 2 O 2 formation. As a result, Cs-OCN achieved an H 2 O 2 production rate of 24,805 μmol g -1 h -1 , along with an apparent quantum yield (AQY) of 49.3% at 420 nm. This study provides a possible dopant-mediated Lewis-acidity regulation strategy for efficient solar-to-chemicals conversion.

title: Orchestrating hydrogen bond networks in linker-edited COFs for accelerated proton-coupled H2O2 photosynthesis
abstract: The sluggish kinetics of the water oxidation reaction (WOR) remain the primary bottleneck for photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production. Beyond traditional band-structure engineering, modulating the pore microenvironment to synchronize mass transfer and charge kinetics is crucial yet challenging. Here, we report a channel-wall engineering strategy by incorporating urea linkages into a covalent organic framework (urea-COF) to create ordered, hydrophilic hydrogen-bond networks. Theoretical and kinetic analyses reveal that these networks function as a proton highway, facilitating ultrafast Grotthuss-type proton transfer and lowering the activation barrier. Consequently, the urea-COF delivers a highly efficient H 2 O 2 production rate of 4104 μmol g -1 h -1 with an apparent quantum yield of 7.2% at 405 nm, outperforming its imine-counterparts by 2.8-fold. Bridging molecular design with macroscopic application, a buoyant triphase reactor was developed for sustainable water disinfection. Techno-economic analysis demonstrates a competitive levelized cost of $14.6 kg -1 , confirming its potential for real-world deployment. This work highlights the critical role of interfacial proton flux management in advancing the frontiers of decentralized solar utilization.

title: Modular synthesis of unsymmetrical all-carbon tetrasubstituted alkenes via Pd-catalyzed multi-component coupling
abstract: Tetrasubstituted alkenes constitute privileged architectures in material science, biomedicine, and chemistry. However, achieving their stereocontrolled synthesis-especially for molecules with four distinct substituents-remains a formidable challenge, as conventional methods lack the necessary modularity and stereoselectivity. Herein, we report a palladium-catalyzed three-component cascade reaction that directly couples alkynyl tetracoordinate boron compounds with two different aryl halides in a single vessel. The reaction proceeds through initial coupling with one aryl halide to form an alkenylboron intermediate, followed by a second Suzuki-type coupling with the other aryl halide. This strategy effectively addresses long-standing challenges of chemoselectivity and byproduct formation in the synthesis of tetrasubstituted alkenes. It enables the modular assembly of unsymmetrical tetrasubstituted alkenes with precise control over chemo-, regio-, and stereoselectivity. Notably, this method provides access even to the most challenging targets bearing four distinct substituents in a stereodefined manner. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions, exhibits exceptional functional group tolerance, and accommodates a broad substrate scope (>100 examples). Significantly, several derivatives exhibit aggregation-induced emission (AIE) with a distinct bathochromic shift (red-shift) in the solid state, underscoring the potential of this unique alkene architecture for developing solid-state red-emitters. Furthermore, we demonstrate the concise synthesis of the pharmaceutical agents Toremifene and Tamoxifen using this method. This work establishes a versatile and practical platform for accessing these coveted architectures, with broad implications for synthetic chemistry and materials science.

title: Rewriting the code of bone repair: a bioelectric approach
3d orbital occupancy regulation stabilizes *CO2δ− intermediate for efficient urea electrosynthesis
abstract: Electrosynthesis of urea via C-N coupling of CO 2 with nitrate (NO 3 - ) has emerged as a fascinating energy-efficient technology. However, the inherent disparity in activation barriers between CO 2 and NO 3 - severely impedes efficient C-N bond formation. Herein, we present an unconventional CO 2 -mediated C-N coupling pathway enabled by d-orbital modulation of Cu single atoms anchored on titanium carbide (Cu SACs /TiC). Combined theoretical calculations and in-situ spectroscopic analyses reveal that strong electronic metal-support interaction (EMSI) downshifts the d band center of Cu SACs , while spin-charge injection increases Cu [Formula: see text] occupancy from t 2g 6 e g 3 to t 2g 6 e g 4 . This electronic reconfiguration of Cu SACs d-orbital enables controlled electron transfer into the CO 2 π* orbitals, facilitating the electron-transfer (ET) to generate *CO 2 δ - intermediate. Simultaneously, the bonding orbitals of *NO 2 generated on the TiC directly couple with the antibonding orbital of *CO 2 δ - , promoting C-N bond formation toward urea. Consequently, the optimal Cu SACs /TiC delivers an outstanding C selectivity of 97.8%, along with an excellent Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 50.1% and yield of 558.8 μg h -1 mg cat -1 for urea production in the electrolyte of 0.05 mol L -1 KNO 3 and 0.1 mol L -1 KHCO 3 . This work highlights a unique C-N coupling pathway via d-orbital engineering for efficient electrochemical C-N bond formation from CO 2 and nitrogenous feedstocks.

title: Coincident evolution of glaciers and proglacial lakes across the Himalaya
Endothelial BACE1 impairs insulin signaling to drive cerebral small vessel disease and stroke
abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a major cause of stroke and dementia, yet its molecular etiology remains incompletely understood, and no disease-modifying therapies are currently available. Here, we identify a non-canonical pathogenic mechanism linking β-secretase 1 (BACE1), a therapeutic target for Alzheimer's disease, to vascular insulin resistance. BACE1 was upregulated in the cerebral endothelium of patients with hypertensive arteriopathy and cerebral amyloid angiopathy. The upregulated endothelial BACE1 cleaved the β-subunit of insulin receptor (INSR), disrupting the INSR-Akt-endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) signaling axis required for vascular homeostasis. This disruption occurred early in disease progression in a relevant rodent model of CSVD, the stroke-prone spontaneously hypertensive rat fed a high-salt diet. Treatment with the clinical BACE1 inhibitor elenbecestat (E2609) restored endothelial function, ameliorated cerebrovascular pathology, and significantly reduced stroke incidence. INSR blockade abolished these protective effects, supporting an INSR-dependent mechanism. These findings identify an intersection between neurodegenerative and metabolic pathways in the vasculature and suggest that BACE1 inhibitors, previously abandoned in Alzheimer's disease treatment, may have therapeutic potential for stroke prevention and CSVD therapy.

title: Classification of Phanerozoic oceanic anoxic events
Uneven distribution of surge-induced glacial lake outburst floods across the Third Pole
Oxidized phospholipids: evolution, signaling, cell death, and human diseases
abstract: Oxidized phospholipids (OxPLs) represent a class of molecules generated during evolution that shift from fundamental membrane building-blocks to key signaling mediators, linking lipid metabolism, cellular redox homeostasis and multi-faceted cell-fate control. Generated by both enzymatic and non-enzymatic peroxidation events, OxPLs engage in extensive signaling crosstalk with lyso-phospholipids and oxylipins. The FerroLipid framework describes iron-lipid peroxidation crosstalk to contextualize iron-dependent lipid signaling. OxPLs govern diverse regulated cell-death programs: they act as lipid death signals in apoptosis and ferroptosis, tune ferroptotic outputs through intrinsic antioxidant systems, and exert context-specific modulatory effects on pyroptosis and other cell-death modalities. Beyond cell-death execution, OxPLs signal through pattern-recognition, scavenger and nuclear receptors to orchestrate inflammation, membrane remodeling, phagocytic clearance, autophagy, mitophagy and protein homeostasis. Threshold-dependent accumulation of OxPLs drives pathological processes across neurodegenerative, metabolic, cardiovascular, neoplastic and infectious diseases; their disease-specific molecular signatures confer potential as both diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Redox phospholipidomics coupled with mass-spectrometry imaging enables accurate, species-resolved profiling of distinct OxPL species. Multiple pharmacological approaches and gene-editing interventions have demonstrated tangible translational prospects for OxPL-oriented therapy. This review synthesizes existing knowledge of OxPL biology from evolutionary origins and signaling mechanisms to disease relevance, analytical tools and therapeutic opportunities. It highlights major unresolved research bottlenecks and provides a solid conceptual foundation for advancing lipid-targeted treatments for complex human disorders.

title: Targeting pericytes to overcome resistance to tumor anti-angiogenic therapy

Corrigendum to “Synergistic optimization of pore structure and hydrophilicity for an ultrathin, high-safety composite diaphragm toward high-current, durable alkaline water electrolysis” [Sci. Bull. 71(15) (2026) 3937–3950]
Ion-selective electrodes for in vivo applications in animal models: from single-time measurement to long-term monitoring
Pressure-intensified co-electrolysis of CO and plastic waste for sustainable carboxylate production
Molecular response diversity of dissolved organic matter under ocean warming
abstract: How dissolved organic matter (DOM) composition varies along ocean temperature gradients is critical for understanding its role in future ocean carbon cycling. Here, we use a highly resolved dataset of over 800 DOM samples covering the surface waters to the deep Atlantic, Southern, and Pacific oceans to examine DOM thermal responses, defined as temperature-associated changes in DOM molecular relative abundance. Towards deeper waters, both response strength (i.e., net response) and diversity (i.e., variation among molecules) decline. However, these two dimensions show opposite trends with apparent concentrations of more recalcitrant molecules: the net response becomes more negative, while response diversity increases. Consistent with this divergence, response diversity is more strongly associated with photochemical molecular signatures than is the response strength, suggesting a possible photochemical imprint on persistent DOM.
