By projecting global ocean thermal responses from 1950 to 2020 using environmental temperature, salinity, and radiation, we predict that increases in response diversity are most apparent below 1000 m, which could potentially increase the recalcitrant deep-ocean carbon sink. These findings identify molecular response diversity as a distinct dimension of DOM responses to ocean warming and highlight the potential role of photochemical imprints in shaping marine DOM persistence under climate change.

title: Exploiting nano-deliquescence for ambient dry welding of gold nanostructures
Complications and effectiveness at 3 years in women treated for pelvic organ prolapse with transvaginal mesh repair: results from the PRIMES Registry in China
p-n Heterojunction engineering in Na3V2(PO4)2F3-based cathode: space-charge boosted carrier kinetics for high-rate and wide-temperature sodium-ion batteries
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) stand as promising candidates for grid-scale energy storage, with Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 2 F 3 (NVPF) emerging as a competitive cathode material owing to its robust Na superionic conductor (NASICON)-type structure and high operating voltage. However, its practical application is severely hindered by intrinsically low electronic conductivity and sluggish Na + diffusion kinetics. Herein, we report an in-situ phase transition strategy to construct a p-n heterostructure within NVPF-based cathodes, integrating n-type NVPF and p-type Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 (NVP) via thermally induced fluorine loss. This unique heterostructure harnesses the atomic-scale interfacial space-charge effect to establish a built-in electric field, which serves as a core driving force for boosted carrier kinetics. The inherent Fermi-level disparity between NVPF and NVP triggers directional carrier diffusion, forming a space-charge region that synergistically enhances bulk electronic conductivity and lowers the Na + migration barriers. The resulting pn-NVPF-based cathode delivers exceptional electrochemical performance with a reversible capacity of 61.4 mAh g -1 at an ultrahigh rate of 50 C (1 C = 128 mA g -1 ), 80% state of charge achieved in merely 3.5 min at 10 C, and 83.3% capacity retention after 10,000 cycles at 10 C. Notably, it maintains stable operation over an extreme temperature range of - 40 to 60 °C. When assembled into a hard carbon//pn-NVPF full cell, it retains 94.2% capacity after 100 cycles under fast-charge (3 C)/slow-discharge (0.2 C) conditions and delivers a high energy density of 397.6 Wh kg -1 at 0.2 C. This study establishes the space-charge effect as a versatile design principle for overcoming the dual kinetic bottlenecks in electrode materials, offering new insights into the development of high-performance SIBs.

title: ROS1 function in epigenetic regulation: from enzymatic activity to chromatin-gated targeting via LHP1-centered regulatory circuits

Global lithium isotopes reveal climatic and topographic thresholds in silicate weathering

Transcending conventional boundaries via three-dimensional architectures: redefining structure-function relationships with bioinspired insights
A glimpse of dark matter in LUX-ZEPLIN?
Structural encoding of mechanics and bioactivity in a multilevel helical bacterial cellulose scaffold for anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
X-ray scattering insights into crystallization, degradation, and heterogeneity of mixed-halide perovskites
abstract: Mixed-halide perovskites have emerged as indispensable light absorbers for high-efficiency tandem photovoltaics, yet their compositional complexity and processing sensitivity demand advanced structural characterization to elucidate film formation, evolution, and degradation across multiple length and time scales. While previous reviews primarily focus on basic tutorials or specific topics like crystallization and degradation, a systematic methodological framework for advanced X-ray platforms remains absent. This review bridges this critical gap by establishing a comprehensive spatiotemporal characterization paradigm. Methodologically, it shifts analysis from static observations to dynamic, nanoscale-resolved, multimodal investigations, enabling mechanistic links among film formation, operational evolution, and heterogeneity-driven segregation. Furthermore, we highlight critical forward-looking perspectives, including the integration of artificial intelligence assisted automated analysis, upscaled in situ characterization setups, and multimodal characterization. This review aims to equip the community with advanced structural-probing strategies to overcome the bottlenecks of tandem photovoltaics and accelerate their commercialization.

title: Spectra evidence for the Kitaev interaction and unconventional plateau phase in a spin-1 honeycomb magnet
Moiré superlattices: from low to high dimensions
Flood warnings face a new challenge from hidden glacier water
Engineered nanobiotechnology for cancer immunotherapy
abstract: Despite the clinical success of immune checkpoint blockade and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies, solid tumors frequently remain poorly responsive due to multi-step failures in initiating, maintaining, and executing immune responses in vivo. Overcoming these barriers requires organizing immune cues into productive biological relationships rather than simply intensifying systemic immune stimulation. This review examines how engineered nanobiotechnology addresses this central challenge by spatially and temporally coordinating key immune processes. Adopting a biology-driven and engineering-enhanced perspective, we analyze nanoscale interventions across four critical phases of antitumor immunity. Immune initiation engineering optimizes antigen processing and localized delivery to promote productive T-cell priming. To sustain these responses, targeted nanosystems reprogram lymphocytes and myeloid cells toward functional effector states in vivo. At the cellular interface, engineered platforms spatially coordinate immune recognition and effector engagement, while tumor microenvironment (TME) engineering remodels the suppressive niche to support tumor-specific immune activation. By organizing these advances through a process-centered engineering framework, we elucidate how nanobiotechnology can convert otherwise localized, transient, or poorly coordinated immune stimulation into integrated antitumor immunity. Finally, we discuss emerging clinical examples and translational requirements, highlighting how pharmacodynamic immune readouts, patient stratification, and manufacturable designs will drive next-generation nano-immunotherapies toward solid-tumor treatment.

MeCP2 stabilizes the glucocorticoid system in active chromatin regions
abstract: Methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MeCP2), a key epigenetic factor regulating gene expression via DNA/chromatin interactions, causes Rett syndrome when dysfunctional. However, its regulatory mechanisms at the pan-tissue and multi-omics levels remain poorly understood. Here, we constructed comprehensive pan-tissue transcriptional profiles and chromatin accessibility profiles from wild-type and Mecp2-knockout mice. Integrative analyses revealed that glucocorticoid (GC)-induced genes (GIGs) exhibited global hyperactivation following Mecp2 knockout, highlighting a crucial role for MeCP2 in maintaining GC signaling homeostasis. Through innovative single-cell multi-omics profiling of the nervous system, we found that GIG dysregulation primarily disrupts neural homeostasis via non-neuronal cells. Mechanistically, we uncovered a dual regulatory mode of MeCP2: (1) limiting NR3C1 occupancy at GIG cis-regulatory elements in active chromatin regions, and (2) disrupting NR3C1 interaction with its coactivator NCOA1. Importantly, pharmacologically suppressing aberrant GC system activation ameliorated pathological phenotypes and significantly prolonged survival in Mecp2-knockout mice. Our study demonstrates the critical pathological role of hyperactivated GC signaling in the multisystem disturbances of Mecp2-knockout mice and suggests potential therapeutic targets for Rett syndrome.

Defect inheritance upgrading of spent LiMn2O4 to disordered rock-salt cathodes: stabilized oxygen redox enabled by regulating electron localization

The ZmGPAT6–ZmMPK2/7–ZmPIP2;1 fine-regulated module confers salt-alkali tolerance via controlling H2O2 transport in maize
abstract: Soil salinization and alkalization represent major abiotic stresses that severely constrain global agricultural sustainability, crop productivity, and food security. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying plant adaptation to both stresses are far from being fully resolved. Here, we identify a salt-alkali stress-responsive gene, ZmGPAT6 , encoding a glycerol-3-phosphate acyltransferase (GPAT) with dual enzymatic activities of acyltransferase and phosphatase. ZmGPAT6 catalyzes the production of lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) and monoacylglycerol (MAG), resulting in the decline of phosphatidic acid (PA). PA binds to and activates ZmMPK2 and ZmMPK7 kinases, which interact with and phosphorylate the aquaporin ZmPIP2;1, thereby facilitating H 2 O 2 transport in maize leaves and roots. However, ZmGPAT6 interacts with and directly dephosphorylates ZmMPK2/7 and ZmPIP2;1, consequently inhibiting ZmPIP2;1-driven H 2 O 2 transport. Both salt and alkali stresses induce ZmGPAT6 expression in maize leaves and roots, leading to reduced PA accumulation and thus decreasing the phosphorylation level of ZmPIP2;1 by ZmMPK2/7. Simultaneously, the stress-induced accumulation of ZmGPAT6 enhances the dephosphorylation levels of ZmMPK2/7 and ZmPIP2;1. Under both stress conditions, the ZmGPAT6 – ZmMPK2/7 – ZmPIP2;1 module dually restricts H 2 O 2 transport, leading to H 2 O 2 over-accumulation in leaves and roots and impairing maize growth. Our findings reveal a direct linkage between ZmGPAT6-mediated lipid metabolism and ZmMPK2/7-driven phosphorylation of ZmPIP2;1 required for H 2 O 2 transport, thus offering novel insights and potential genetic targets for improving salt-alkali tolerance in maize.

title: Lewis acid-base chemistry enables ultrastable zinc iodine battery through overall iodine species management
abstract: Managing the complex iodine species (I 2 , I − , and I 3 − ) with their conflicting chemisorption preferences and sluggish conversion kinetics remains a critical challenge in aqueous zinc-iodine batteries. Herein, we address this challenge by activating a pair of Lewis acid-base active sites (B/N) that enable specific chemisorption of each iodine species, effectively suppress the polyiodide shuttle effect, and simultaneously enhance the conversion kinetics between I 2 /I − . As proof of concept, a B/N co-doped porous carbon (NBC) host was successfully synthesized via a simple co-pyrolysis strategy. In situ spectroscopic analyses, electrochemical tests, and theoretical calculations collectively reveal, at the molecular level, that the Lewis acid-base active site in NBC reduces the activation energy for the iodine redox reaction and accelerates the conversion kinetics. Consequently, the NBC/I 2 cathode delivers a rate capacity of 139.4 mA h g −1 at 5.0 A g −1 along with stable cycling performance of 139.8 mA h g −1 at 1.0 A g −1 over 1000 cycles under iodine loading of 6.0 mg cm 2 , as well as a low self-discharge performance. This work systematically elucidates the role of Lewis acid-base sites in the full-process management of iodine species and provides a perspective for designing highly catalytic host materials in conversion-type energy storage systems.

title: Toward neuromorphic photonics with strong exciton–photon coupling in 2D and quasi-2D hybrid perovskites

Discriminating gap symmetries of superconducting La3Ni2O7
